info.title: Casap API
info.description: Public API for dispute creation and management. Recommended flow: List Accounts -> List Disputable Transactions -> Eligibility Check -> Get Dispute Reasons -> Get Questionnaire -> Create Dispute -> Upload Files (optional). List Member Disputes and Get Dispute Status power the member's dispute screens.

get.description: Returns the accounts the member holds. Each entry carries an accountUuid to send back, unchanged, as the account_uuid on List Disputable Transactions and the Eligibility Check. Use description as the display label in an account picker. account_type filters to one or more account types (repeat the query param); omit it to receive every type. Jointly held accounts are included, with holderType describing the ownership; no other holder's details are ever returned. This is the only endpoint whose customer_uuid also accepts the member's encrypted tax id — see "Encrypting the tax id" in the Disputes API (Self-Service) introduction.

parameters.name: customerUuid
parameters.description:
customer_uuid accepts either form of the member identifier: one Casap
already issued (returned as-is), or the member's tax id encrypted with the
org's Casap-issued public key (RSA-OAEP with SHA-256 as both the OAEP and
MGF1 digest; base64-encode, then percent-encode). See "Encrypting the tax
id" in the Disputes API (Self-Service) introduction for common pitfalls.
Every other RPC's customer_uuid only accepts the identifier this endpoint
resolves to.

parameters.name: accountType
parameters.description:
account_type narrows the result to one or more of the listed account
types (e.g. debit only, or debit and credit explicitly). Leave empty to
receive every type.

get.description: Returns full detail for a single dispute: current status, a human-readable status message, resolution deadline, and a chronological timeline of events (most recent first). Use this to power the dispute detail/status screen.

application/json.statusMessage: Your claim is in progress. You received $132.88

post.description: Files the dispute. Send the transactionId values from List Disputable Transactions in transaction_ids, the customer info, the selected dispute reason, and the questionnaire answers as question_uuid/answer pairs. Returns a DisputeSummary with the dispute's uuid (needed for Upload Files), shortId, resolutionDeadline, and any initial actions (e.g. issue provisional credit). Provide exactly one of transaction_ids or transaction_details; full transaction_details bodies remain supported for existing integrations.

get.description: Returns the member's recent transactions that can be disputed; ineligible ones (too old, wrong status, already disputed) are filtered out. Each entry carries its payment rail (the full transaction type) and two flags, disputable and disputeInProgress, that tell your UI whether the member can select it. Send the returned transactionId values, unchanged, to the Eligibility Check and Create Dispute.

parameters.name: customerUuid
parameters.description:
customer_uuid is the member identifier returned by ListAccounts. The
encrypted tax-id form is not accepted here.

parameters.name: accountType
parameters.description:
account_type is the account's account_type, from its matching ListAccounts
entry. Optional; passing it makes the lookup faster.

get.description: Required step between transaction selection and the reasons screen. Checks that each selected transaction is eligible — including the org's own disputability rules — and that the selection uses a single payment rail and a single card. On failure, returns one structured error per failed rule with a machine-readable code and a member-facing message, so the member can adjust their selection without leaving the flow. See "Eligibility error codes" in the Disputes API (Self-Service) introduction for the full list and recommended UI handling.

errors.message: Please select transactions of the same type. You cannot mix ACH and Debit transactions in a single dispute.
This transaction is already part of an open dispute.

parameters.name: customerUuid
parameters.description:
customer_uuid is the member identifier returned by ListAccounts. The
encrypted tax-id form is not accepted here.

parameters.name: transactionDates
parameters.description:
Optional lookup hint: transaction_dates[i] is the approximate date of
transaction_ids[i], matched +/-1 day; only the date portion is used.
Providing it speeds the lookup; omitting it or getting it wrong never
changes the result. May be shorter than transaction_ids; missing entries
fall back to an unscoped lookup.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of disputes for a given customer. Each entry includes the dispute short ID, total disputed amount, and open/closed status. Does not include transaction-level detail — use Get Dispute Status for that. Default: 10 most recent disputes; maximum: 30 per request. Only disputes created in the last six months are returned, newest first. The window is based on creation date, so an older dispute is not listed even if it is still open.

parameters.name: customerUuid
parameters.description: required; the member identifier returned by ListAccounts (the encrypted tax-id form is not accepted here)

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: default 10, max 30; larger values are capped rather than rejected

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: opaque cursor returned as next_page_token by a prior call; empty for the first page

parameters.name: statusFilter
parameters.description:
Optional status filter. DISPUTE_STATUS_UNKNOWN (the default) returns all
disputes; OPEN or CLOSED restrict the result accordingly.

get.description: Returns the intake questionnaire for the selected dispute reason and transaction context. Each question includes a unique questionUuid, the input type to render, and allowed answer options. The member's questionnaire answers determine the specific sub-reason. Submit question_uuid/answer pairs in Create Dispute.

questions.questionText: When did you first notice the unauthorized transaction?

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description:
- DISPUTE_REASON_ACH_ISSUE: Unauthorized ACH debit. Other ACH problems use the more specific
DISPUTE_REASON_ACH_* values.
 - DISPUTE_REASON_ACH_CREDIT_ISSUE: Dispute about an ACH credit (incoming or outgoing credit entry), as

get.description: Returns the set of applicable parent-level dispute reason categories for the selected transactions. The member selects one of these categories; the specific sub-reason is determined downstream by the member's answers to the intake questionnaire. Call this after the Eligibility Check passes.

post.description: Attaches a supporting document to an existing dispute. Optional; requires the dispute uuid returned by Create Dispute, so it can only run after creation. Returns the file_uuid of the stored file.

PartialApproval carries the amount an agent approved when approving for less
than the disputed total. It is the amount the member keeps, not the amount
debited back.

transactionPostedDate.description:
transaction_posted_date is the date the analyst indicates the
transaction actually posted, for denial reasons that describe a
delay between the transaction date and its posting.

actionsGetAccountNumberModalAction.description:
GetAccountNumberModalAction opens the account-number edit modal. The edit fans
out to every transaction in the dispute, so the modal is scoped to the dispute
rather than any individual transaction.

api_publicdtoDisputeReason.description:
DisputeReason is the dispute reason category. GetDisputeReasons returns the
applicable parent categories; the specific sub-reason is resolved
server-side from the questionnaire answers at Create time, so callers only
ever submit a parent reason. Legacy reason values are normalized to this set
before they reach the API, so these are the only values integrators see.

 - DISPUTE_REASON_ACH_ISSUE: Unauthorized ACH debit. Other ACH problems use the more specific
DISPUTE_REASON_ACH_* values.
 - DISPUTE_REASON_ACH_CREDIT_ISSUE: Dispute about an ACH credit (incoming or outgoing credit entry), as
opposed to the ACH_ISSUE_* family, which covers consumer debit disputes.

commonChargebackEligibility.description:
ChargebackEligibility reports whether a chargeback can be filed for a
transaction. UNKNOWN is the default and means no verdict has been reached —
the inputs were incomplete, or the rules produced no definitive answer. It is
distinct from NOT_ELIGIBLE, which is a decision that no rights exist.

isFee.description: is_fee marks a fee-shaped transaction (standalone core fee or embedded fee row).

feeId.description: fee_id is the processor fee identifier used to reverse the fee (e.g. Galileo fee_id).

questionnaire.description: TODO: Quick hack to get questionnaire out sooner. Needs type safety.

dtoAccountType.description:
AccountType splits accounts the way the core banking systems do: deposit and
share accounts, whose transactions are debit, versus credit card and loan
accounts, whose transactions are credit.

dtoAttachedFile.description: AttachedFile is a member-uploaded file attached to a dispute.

rail.description:
rail is the transaction's full TransactionType, not a grouping. Use it to
tell rails apart: transactions on different rails cannot be disputed
together.

cardLast4.description:
card_last4 is the last 4 digits of the card used, when the transaction is
card-based and a card record is available. Empty otherwise (e.g. ACH).

dtoDisputableTransaction.description:
DisputableTransaction is a customer transaction annotated with whether it can
currently be disputed. It is returned by the "List Disputable Transactions"
endpoint.

maxDaysSinceTxn.description: Transaction eligibility windows, in days since the transaction settled.

abuserLookbackDays.description: Lookback window, in days, used for dispute-abuser detection.

hiddenTransactionTypes.description:
Transaction rails hidden/disabled for self-service disputing, mapped from
the org's configured OFX transaction-type codes onto TransactionType. A
code with no TransactionType equivalent is silently dropped.

maxTransactionsPerDispute.description:
Maximum number of transactions allowed in a single dispute. 0 means no
limit is configured. Display-only: not enforced server-side.

palette.description:
Visual color tokens for Lumin to skin their own dispute UI. Absent if the
org has no iframe branding configured. Copy/text branding (blocker text,
claim text, etc.) is intentionally out of scope here — Lumin owns its own
UI copy.

dtoDisputeConfig.description:
DisputeConfig is the partner-facing projection of an org's dispute
configuration. It is a public view over the SAME underlying org config data
served by the internal org-config endpoint
(GET /v1/organizations/{uuid}/config), exposing only the fields the
self-service dispute flow needs.

disputedAmount.title: total disputed across the dispute's transactions

dtoDisputeListItem.description:
DisputeListItem is a member-facing summary row for the dispute-history list
(ListMemberDisputes). It intentionally omits transaction-level detail — use
Get Dispute Status for the full DisputeDetail.

dtoDisputeReasonOption.description:
DisputeReasonOption is an applicable dispute reason for a given set of
transactions, paired with default customer-facing display language.

disputeReason.description:
dispute_reason pairs reason with its customer-facing display message,
matching the shape GetDisputeReasons returns. reason is kept as-is for
existing integrators.

uuid.description:
The transaction identifier: the id supplied at Create or, when Casap
looked the transaction up server-side, the id it resolved to. An id that
is omitted or repeated within one request is replaced with a generated
one. Use it to join disputes back to your records;
TimelineTransaction.uuid carries the same value. Unlike the dispute uuid,
it does not change when a dispute is reopened.

requiredActions.description:
What Casap currently needs from the member for this transaction, as of
this snapshot. Unlike DisputeSummary.actions (a cumulative history of
actions triggered over the dispute's life), an empty list here means
nothing is currently outstanding, and a value drops out once it's
resolved or the transaction closes.

dtoEligibilityError.description:
EligibilityError describes one reason a dispute selection is ineligible.
transaction_ids identifies the offending transactions when the error is
transaction-scoped; it is empty for member-scoped errors.

dtoEligibilityErrorCode.description:
EligibilityErrorCode is the machine-readable reason a selection is
ineligible. Transaction-scoped codes (RAIL_MISMATCH, CARD_MISMATCH, and the
TRANSACTION_* values) name the offending ids in transaction_ids; the member
can adjust their selection. MEMBER_INELIGIBLE is member-scoped:
transaction_ids is empty and no selection change helps. See "Eligibility
error codes" in the Disputes API (Self-Service) introduction for handling
guidance.

 - RAIL_MISMATCH: The selection mixes payment rails (e.g. ACH and Debit) that cannot be
disputed together.
 - TRANSACTION_INELIGIBLE: Deprecated: no longer returned. Match the specific TRANSACTION_* codes
instead.
 - MEMBER_INELIGIBLE: The member cannot file any dispute right now (e.g. classified as a
dispute abuser), regardless of selection.
 - TRANSACTION_NOT_FOUND: A selected id matches no transaction on the member's account (stale,
mistyped, or superseded).
 - TRANSACTION_NOT_SETTLED: A selected transaction has not settled yet; it can be disputed once it
does.
 - TRANSACTION_ALREADY_DISPUTED: A selected transaction is already part of an open dispute.
 - TRANSACTION_OUTSIDE_ELIGIBILITY_WINDOW: A selected transaction is older than the org's configured window for
self-service disputes.
 - CARD_MISMATCH: The selection spans more than one card.
 - TRANSACTION_NOT_DISPUTABLE: A selected transaction is excluded by the org's disputability rules
(e.g. a transaction type the org does not allow to be disputed online).

dtoInputType.description: InputType is the UI input control a questionnaire question should render.

accountUuid.description:
account_uuid is the identifier every other endpoint expects. Despite the
name it is not a UUID: it is the member id followed by the zero-padded
share id (member_id + share_id below). Echo it back verbatim rather than
reconstructing it.

customerUuid.description:
customer_uuid is the canonical member identifier this account resolved to,
suitable for the customer_uuid argument on the other endpoints.

memberId.description: member_id is the member/CIF number: the leading component of account_uuid.

shareId.description:
share_id is the account's id within the member (share or loan), zero-padded
to 4 digits: the trailing component of account_uuid.

description.description:
description is the account's core description, falling back to its
nickname. Suitable as the display label in an account picker.

holderType.description:
holder_type is this member's ownership of the account, e.g. "Primary",
"Joint", or "Beneficiary". Not a closed set: some core banking systems pass
their own relationship text through verbatim, so new values can appear
without notice.

openedAt.description:
opened_at is the epoch timestamp the account was opened, 0 when the core
does not report a parseable open date.

dtoMemberAccount.description:
MemberAccount is a single account a member holds, as returned by "List
Accounts".

parentQuestionUuid.description:
parent_question_uuid is the question_uuid of the question whose answer
gates the follow-up. The server guarantees it is never empty and always
references a question in the same response.

parentAnswerValues.description:
parent_answer_values are the parent QuestionOption.value entries that
reveal the follow-up; any one of them satisfies the condition. The server
guarantees at least one non-empty value.

dtoQuestionCondition.description:
QuestionCondition is one way a conditional follow-up question is revealed:
the answer to the question identified by parent_question_uuid is one of
parent_answer_values.

questionUuid.title: stable id; pass back in Create

options.title: present for RADIO/DROPDOWN/CHECKBOX; empty for TEXT/DATE

required.description:
required is true for questions shown unconditionally; answer them on every
submission. Conditional follow-ups have required = false: answer them when
one of their conditions is met.

dtoQuestionDefinition.description:
QuestionDefinition is a single intake question to present to the customer.
The questionnaire is a conditional tree flattened into an ordered list: each
question_uuid appears exactly once, and a question with a non-empty
conditions list is a follow-up that should only be shown once one of its
conditions is satisfied.

dtoQuestionOption.description: QuestionOption is an allowed answer value for a choice-style question.

dtoRequiredAction.description:
RequiredAction is something Casap currently needs from the member on a
transaction. New values are added here as new situations need to be
surfaced explicitly, instead of one purpose-built boolean per situation.

dtoTimelineEvent.description:
TimelineEvent is one entry in the member-facing dispute timeline: a
human-readable milestone with an optional detail sub-message, its timestamp,
and the transaction(s) it relates to (empty for dispute-level events).

dtoTimelineEventType.description:
TimelineEventType is the lifecycle stage a timeline entry represents. Only
member-facing events appear on the timeline.

 - TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPE_INFORMATION_REQUESTED: Casap asked the member for documents or information. Requests directed at
the financial institution are not shown.
 - TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPE_EVIDENCE_SUBMITTED: The member uploaded evidence. Files uploaded by an agent are not shown.

uuid.description:
Matches DisputedTransaction.uuid on the same dispute; use it to attach a
timeline entry to a transaction.

dtoTimelineTransaction.description:
TimelineTransaction is a disputed transaction referenced by a timeline event,
hydrated with the member-facing detail needed to render the entry.

eventsAddTransactions.description:
AddTransactions appends one or more transactions to an already-created dispute.
Reuses TransactionDetail so callers (including fee pickers) can submit any txn shape.

isStrict.title: If enabled then more strict validations will fail the event

text.description: Deprecated: superseded by the per-network sub-messages below.

network.description: Deprecated: network is derived from the transaction; use form instead.

form.description:
Generic key-value form payload submitted by the user.
Keys: fraudType, issuerGenAuth, rolTransactionId, arn.

eventsUpdateChargebackEligibility.description:
UpdateChargebackEligibility records a change in a transaction's chargeback
eligibility. The producer stamps previous_eligibility from the value it read,
so replaying the stream reconstructs the full transition rather than only the
latest verdict.

previousCreatedTimestamp.description:
The value being replaced, so the audit row can render the correction rather
than only its result.

eventsUpdateFee.title: TODO (andrew): can deprecate and consolidate to UpdateAmount so the terminology is consistent

eventsUpdateMerchantCredit.description:
UpdateMerchantCredit records the key of a matching merchant-issued credit
on the dispute transaction. Used by the agentic pre-resolution node.

eventsUpdateNetworkDetails.description:
UpdateNetworkDetails sets the network and network-specific identifiers on a
transaction. Used by automation job actions (e.g. before filing a chargeback)
to record the VROL transaction ID from the network response, and by the
dispute details UI to submit user-provided network identifiers.

eventsUpdateTransactionDate.description:
UpdateTransactionDate carries a dev-user override of a transaction's
timestamp, used to bring simulator test data inside network filing windows.

eventsUpdateVerifiCase.description:
UpdateVerifiCase records a Verifi case-status transition detected by the
verifi-sync poller. verifi_case carries the case exactly as the poller
fetched it, so the handling spec writes the case facet without a second
vendor call. It is transport only: the recorded dispute event is the status
transition, not the case payload.

eventsUpdateWarranty.description: UpdateWarranty carries a dev-user override of a check transaction's warranty.

fileStage.description: Optional: default file stage to apply to uploaded files.

@type.description:
Identifies the type of the serialized Protobuf message with a URI reference
consisting of a prefix ending in a slash and the fully-qualified type name.

Example: type.googleapis.com/google.protobuf.StringValue

This string must contain at least one `/` character, and the content after
the last `/` must be the fully-qualified name of the type in canonical
form, without a leading dot. Do not write a scheme on these URI references
so that clients do not attempt to contact them.

The prefix is arbitrary and Protobuf implementations are expected to
simply strip off everything up to and including the last `/` to identify
the type. `type.googleapis.com/` is a common default prefix that some
legacy implementations require. This prefix does not indicate the origin of
the type, and URIs containing it are not expected to respond to any
requests.

All type URL strings must be legal URI references with the additional
restriction (for the text format) that the content of the reference
must consist only of alphanumeric characters, percent-encoded escapes, and
characters in the following set (not including the outer backticks):
`/-.~_!$&()*+,;=`. Despite our allowing percent encodings, implementations
should not unescape them to prevent confusion with existing parsers. For
example, `type.googleapis.com%2FFoo` should be rejected.

In the original design of `Any`, the possibility of launching a type
resolution service at these type URLs was considered but Protobuf never
implemented one and considers contacting these URLs to be problematic and
a potential security issue. Do not attempt to contact type URLs.

protobufAny.description:
`Any` contains an arbitrary serialized protocol buffer message along with a
URL that describes the type of the serialized message.

In its binary encoding, an `Any` is an ordinary message; but in other wire
forms like JSON, it has a special encoding. The format of the type URL is
described on the `type_url` field.

Protobuf APIs provide utilities to interact with `Any` values:

- A 'pack' operation accepts a message and constructs a generic `Any` wrapper
  around it.
- An 'unpack' operation reads the content of an `Any` message, either into an
  existing message or a new one. Unpack operations must check the type of the
  value they unpack against the declared `type_url`.
- An 'is' operation decides whether an `Any` contains a message of the given
  type, i.e. whether it can 'unpack' that type.

The JSON format representation of an `Any` follows one of these cases:

- For types without special-cased JSON encodings, the JSON format
  representation of the `Any` is the same as that of the message, with an
  additional `@type` field which contains the type URL.
- For types with special-cased JSON encodings (typically called 'well-known'
  types, listed in https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/#any), the
  JSON format representation has a key `@type` which contains the type URL
  and a key `value` which contains the JSON-serialized value.

The text format representation of an `Any` is like a message with one field
whose name is the type URL in brackets. For example, an `Any` containing a
`foo.Bar` message may be written `[type.googleapis.com/foo.Bar] { a: 2 }`.

protobufNullValue.description:
Represents a JSON `null`.

`NullValue` is a sentinel, using an enum with only one value to represent
the null value for the `Value` type union.

A field of type `NullValue` with any value other than `0` is considered
invalid. Most ProtoJSON serializers will emit a Value with a `null_value` set
as a JSON `null` regardless of the integer value, and so will round trip to
a `0` value.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.

badge.description: Shown on the closed trigger, e.g. a total across the options.

international.title: Whether to format as international number

sharedStyledText.title: if size, color and weight are not set, default to normal

v1CheckDisputeEligibilityResponse.description:
CheckDisputeEligibilityResponse reports whether the member may file the
dispute. eligible is true only when errors is empty. Each error carries a
machine-readable code, a member-facing message, and — for transaction-scoped
codes — the offending transaction ids. A selection can fail several rules at
once; errors then has one entry per rule.

introductoryText.title: html text that will come up as first screen

unauthClaimText.title: text for an extra card in unauth disputes successful submission modal

extraSections.title: text for extra sections in successful submission modal, goes after unauth claim text

transactionDetails.description:
Legacy: full caller-supplied transaction data, still supported for
existing integrations. New integrations should use transaction_ids.
Provide exactly one of the two.

transactionIds.description:
transaction_ids selects the transactions to dispute by id, using the
transaction_id values returned by ListDisputableTransactions. Ids that
fail the eligibility rules (unknown, already disputed, mixed rails) are
rejected. Mutually exclusive with transaction_details.

v1GetDisputeReasonsResponse.description:
GetDisputeReasonsResponse lists the dispute reasons applicable to the
requested transaction(s), each with default customer-facing display language.

statusMessage.description:
status_message is a human-readable summary of the dispute's current state,
for display on the member-facing dispute detail screen.

timeline.description: timeline is the member-facing event history, most recent first.

v1ListAccountsResponse.description:
ListAccountsResponse returns every account the member holds that the org
exposes, each with the account_uuid the rest of the flow expects.

v1ListDisputableTransactionsResponse.description:
ListDisputableTransactionsResponse returns the customer's transactions, each
annotated with whether it can currently be disputed.

nextPageToken.title: empty when there are no further pages

totalCount.title: total disputes matching the scope/filter, across all pages

type.title: Type of account (e.g. "C" for credit, "D" for debit, "ALL" for no discrimination)

names.title: Names of the txn to match (e.g. "Withdrawal by ATM") - comma separated

exceptionWords.title:
Words that should not be matched (e.g. "Withdrawal") - comma separated
(e.g. "Withdrawal by ATM" will not be matched even if "ATM" is in the names)

fileUuid.title: The identifier assigned to the stored file

api_key.description: Bearer token, constructed as base64(org_uuid:secret). Casap provides org_uuid and a static secret during partner onboarding; send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
api_key.name: Authorization
